stanzas: Yo soy un hombre sincero
De donde crece la palma.
Y antes de morirme quiero
Echar mis versos del alma.
Mi verso es de un verde claro
Y de un carmín encendido:
Mi verso es un ciervo herido
Que busca en el monte amparo.
Cultivo una rosa blanca
En julio como enero,
Para el amigo sincero
Que me da su mano franca.
Con los pobres de la tierra
Quiero yo mi suerte echar:
El arroyo de la sierra
Me complace más que el mar.
orig.credit: José Martí, Versos sencillos (1891): the verses the song sets, from poems I, V, XXXIX and III (its refrain, credited to Joseíto Fernández, is not printed)

stanzas: I am an honest man
from where the palm tree grows,
and before I die I want
to pour out the verses of my soul.
My verse is of a light green
and of a burning crimson;
my verse is a wounded deer
that seeks shelter on the mountain.
I grow a white rose
in July as in January
for the true friend
who gives me his open hand.
With the poor of the earth
I want to cast my lot;
the mountain stream
pleases me more than the sea.

notes: These are four quatrains of José Martí's Versos sencillos (New York, 1891), from poems I, V, XXXIX and III, the ones most often sung to the tune. Singers choose freely among Martí's quatrains, which is why recordings differ.
The refrain, "Guantanamera, guajira guantanamera" (country girl from Guantánamo), and the music are 20th-century work credited to Joseíto Fernández and still in copyright: they are not printed here.
